items.title: Alphonse Picou Interview, 1958-04-04
items.q: Well, Burbank... That's another one. That's one of my boys.

ctx.x: Yes. I mean, did he...? I mean, did he...? You didn't play at the same time he did around, did you...? No. No.
What about Albert Burbank? Oh. Well, Burbank... That's another one. That's one of my boys. Yeah, I know that. Yeah, I know that. Yes. Way back, yeah. That's one of my boys.
I noticed that his name is listed as composer of A La Ba. How does he happen to hold the copyright on that? Do you know?

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: So I asked Pico, well he didn't have time to get on all this.

ctx.x: It didn't happen. That was P-Roll. That's about it. So I left there.

Well, who could I try again? Well all the musicians was working. Pico and all those folks, they were working so much they didn't care to be bothered with teaching anybody. So I asked Pico, well he didn't have time to get on all this. The best thing I could do, well there was a fella that some fellas told me about, a fella by the name of Walter DeVoyne. He would play a little clarinet, you know. Well he was a tinsmith, so he was always willing to help somebody, you know. So I had a couple of fellas going to him.…
Did you start with that same method then?

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: We'd make the same variation, but I'd make a second to it, you see. Piku had written out a second for me.

ctx.x: I don't know. You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same.

You wouldn't try to play the same. You wouldn't try to play the same. Like on high society, well, it'd be good. We'd make the same variation, but I'd make a second to it, you see. Piku had written out a second for me. And I don't know what happened to that clarinet. Because that was in Orlando, the band, too. So Piku was there, too? That was after something happened to his saxophone play. He got a regular job and he left the band. He took people in the band. Well, I heard you one night in Washington, in Germany,…
I think I... How would you describe Dick Allen's trombone play? Terrible. Yeah, that's right. Did you ever hear Neely Bonds in the old days play? Yeah, I see.
